text:
Michelle: FYI deploy of scheduler/9f2a1c just triggered a sustained token/sec degradation on continuous-batcher traffic (~18-25%). Canary rollout paused.

Ajay: I can confirm from canary logs. Token/sec drops, queueing latency increases, and average batch size collapses. Looks like the scheduler started favoring a kernel path that forces a copy for short sequences.

Sylvia: CI perf job perf/p95-tokensec flagged it on the merge build. Attach: https://ci.redwood/perf/2154332100/flame.html and artifact /artifacts/perf/2154332100.

ci-bot: perf-check failed: p95 token/sec -22% vs baseline on branch scheduler/merge-9f2a1c. Artifacts: /artifacts/perf/2154332100

Kevin: quick sampled profiler on a hot shard shows hotspots in choose_kernel_variant and continuous_batcher::handoff_spin. Significant time in memcpy paths now.

Andrea: can you paste the minimal repro flags? I want to reproduce locally with the profiler.

Ajay: repro flags I used locally:
```
--batcher-mode=continuous
--scheduler-heuristic=heuristic_v2
--kv-cache=on
--kernel-policy=auto_unified
--perf-trace=stack
```
I also flipped kernel-score weighting (env KERNEL_SCORE_ALPHA=0.7).

Michelle: ran a local quick-run with 15k synthetic requests. p95 token/sec drops mirror prod. Observed batching window shrink from ~60ms -> ~9ms and avg batch size went down ~3x.

Sylvia: flamegraph text summary:
```
choose_kernel_variant 48%
  kernel_score::evaluate 32%
    memcpy/memmove 20%
  unified_kernel_dispatch 16%
continuous_batcher::handoff_spin 20%
  spin_wait 11%
  scheduling_decision 7%
```

Kevin: memcpy dominance suggests the unified kernel path is doing eager preallocation + copy for small seqs. The previous in-place small-seq path avoided that.

Andrea: I bisected the merge. The regression correlates with the kernel-policy refactor in PR 9f2a1c (score weighting change and new unified preference). The diffs around kernel_policy selection (lines ~80-110) flip preference order.

Michelle: can we patch to restore previous preference for in-place on short sequences and rerun canary? If confirmed, we'll revert the merge from rollout.

Ajay: quick patch suggestion:
```
- kernel_policy = PreferUnified
+ kernel_policy = PreferInplaceForShortSeq
```
I'll open a rollback PR and trigger perf-checks.

ci-bot: Opened PR #4729: revert kernel-policy preference change (scheduler). Running perf-checks.

Sylvia: perf-run on the rollback PR looks good: p95 token/sec within 3% of baseline, batch size and queue latency restored.

Kevin: longer-term proposal: add a unit perf test that runs mixed short/long sequences and asserts memcpy_time_ratio < 10%. Also add a telemetry metric kernel_memcpy_bytes to make copy-volume visible in prod dashboards.

Andrea: agreed. I'll add a perf unit (inject synthetic seq distribution) and create ticket #889 for telemetry work.

Michelle: action items:
- Ajay: land rollback PR and stop rollout (in progress) :thumbsup:
- Andrea: add perf unit + create telemetry ticket #889
- Kevin: refine kernel scoring knobs so unified kernel isn't auto-picked for short sequences
- Sylvia: validate canary and confirm perf job stability

Ajay: rollback merged, rollout paused waiting for canary validation.

Sylvia: canary traffic looks stable now, p95 token/sec back to baseline. Marking this incident mitigated. Opening postmortem with timeline, root cause (kernel-policy + scheduler heuristic interaction), and remediation steps.

Michelle: thanks everyone. Keep CI artifacts and profiler traces attached to the postmortem. <3
